title: Crosscut Access, Procurement & Data Playbook
author: Priya Anand
content:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single, operational playbook that unifies access/permission lifecycle, change approval flows, data stewardship requirements, procurement and expense decisions, vendor lifecycle, and travel expense guidance. This document is intended for approvers, requesters, audit reviewers, and operational teams.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood corporate employees, contractors, and temporary accounts across hosted, dedicated, and private product teams.
- Excludes customer-managed systems that are explicitly covered by customer contracts and separate SOC/ISO documentation.

Key Principles
- Least privilege by default: access is granted with the minimum privileges required and is timeboxed where feasible.
- Separation of duties: provisioning, approval, and audit responsibilities should be split across roles.
- Risk-based procurement: vendor onboarding and contract terms reflect data sensitivity and expected exposure.
- Traceable approvals: every entitlement, change, and purchase must be recorded with an approver and a business justification.

1) Access & Permissions (RBAC + Exceptions)

Role model and definitions
- Roles: viewer, operator, developer, service-owner, admin, security-admin.
- Service accounts: life-cycle managed; must be tied to a documented owner and rotate keys every 90 days.

Request & approval process (summary)
1. Requester files an Access Request using the Access Request Form (Confluence form link). Include: reason, justification, expiry date, and related ticket ID.
2. Manager approval required for all human accounts. For admin-level elevation, Manager + Security-Admin approval required.
3. Automation: requests for common roles are auto-provisioned by Identity Orchestration (IAM) if policy conditions met (tenure, team membership).
4. Access is timeboxed by default. Renewal requires a re-request with updated justification.

Temporary emergency access (break-glass)
- Flow: On-call engineer requests emergency elevation via Slack cmd /break-glass -> pager duty alert -> Security-Admin approval within 30 minutes. All sessions captured and reviewed in the next 72-hour postmortem.

Periodic reviews and attestations
- Quarterly attestation by team leads for all active accounts.
- Automated orphaned-account report every 7 days; orphaned accounts are disabled after 14 days until owner is confirmed.

Example IAM policy snippet (simplified YAML for onboarding automation):

```yaml
- principal: team-members:redwood-platform
  role: developer
  ttl_days: 90
  justification_required: true
```

2) Change Management (Infrastructure and Config)

Change categories
- Standard: pre-approved, documented changes with no service-impact (e.g., config tweaks under approved range). Requires ticket and automated CI checks.
- Normal: planned changes with potential impact; requires RFC, testing, and change-window scheduling.
- Emergency: immediate fixes for production-impacting incidents; follow emergency change steps below.

Approval matrix (high-level)
- Low-risk infra change (no user-visible latency/availability impact): Team lead.
- Mid-risk (affects multiple services): Platform lead + SRE signoff.
- High-risk (SLA-affecting): CTO or designated change authority + SRE + Product owner.

Normal change procedure (numbered)
1. Create RFC in the Change Tracker with objectives, rollback plan, risk assessment, test plan, and timeline.
2. Run automated pre-deployment checks: unit tests, integration tests, load smoke tests.
3. Schedule change window and notify stakeholders via Change Calendar (minimum 72hr notice for customer-facing infra).
4. Execute change with runbook steps and a drug-store style checklist.
5. Post-change validation: automated health checks for 30m, manual verification for critical paths.
6. Update documentation and closure in Change Tracker.

Emergency change flow
- Authorization: SRE on-call + service-owner can approve; log the decision in the incident ticket.
- Implement mitigations to reduce blast radius and plan formal RFC within 72 hours for retrospective approval.

3) Data Management & Stewardship

Data classification scheme
- Public: safe to share externally.
- Internal: company information not intended for public distribution.
- Confidential: contains business-critical details (pricing, roadmaps).
- Restricted / PII: regulated personal data or customer-sensitive information.

Handling requirements (summary)
- Restricted data must be stored in approved encrypted buckets, with access restricted via IAM roles and audited every 30 days.
- Default backups are encrypted; retention settings vary by data class (see table).

Retention and deletion table
| Data Class | Minimum Retention | Recommended Deletion Trigger | Storage Location | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Public | 1 year | N/A | Public docs | No encryption required |
| Internal | 2 years | End of fiscal need | Internal storage | Standard encryption |
| Confidential | 7 years | Contract end + 1yr | Encrypted internal storage | Legal review required |
| Restricted/PII | Configured per contract | Deletion on request / legal hold | Encrypted, access-logged | KMS-protected, DLP rules apply |

Data access approval table (summary)
- Standard access: owner team lead.
- Sensitive analytics: owner lead + data steward.
- Cross-team exports of restricted data: Data Steward + Security signoff and a signed DPA with requesting team.

Data incident escalation
1. If data exposure suspected, immediately notify Security via the Security Incident channel and open a Data Incident ticket.
2. Contain: revoke affected credentials, snapshot affected storage, preserve logs.
3. Triage: classify, scope, and notify legal/compliance within 24 hours.
4. Remediate and report: root cause analysis and retrospective published to the security-and-compliance space.

4) Procurement & Expenses (Purchasing Controls)

Finance approval thresholds (compact table)
| Item Type | Threshold (USD) | Approver(s) | Procurement path |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Low-touch software (SaaS, single-seat) | < 5,000 | Team manager | Self-serve via procurement portal |
| Standard SaaS contract | 5,000 - 50,000 | Finance approver + Manager | Procurement ticket + PO |
| Strategic vendor / >50K | > 50,000 | Finance Director + Legal + VP | Formal RFP + Contract review |

Purchase procedure (step-by-step)
1. Initiate procurement request in the Procurement Portal with business justification, budget code, and expected term.
2. Obtain manager approval. If above $5,000, route to Finance approver automatically.
3. Finance validates budget and assigns a PO number.
4. Legal reviews contract if vendor will handle restricted data or the term > 12 months.
5. Procurement confirms SLA, security posture, and onboarding plan.

Card and expense policy highlights
- Company cardholders must submit expense receipts within 14 days.
- Travel bookings should use the preferred vendor portal; exceptions require Manager pre-approval.
- Unapproved personal expenses will be denied and must be reimbursed by the cardholder.

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding

Vendor risk categories
- Low: standard SaaS with no customer data access.
- Medium: vendors with access to internal but non-sensitive data or non-production environments.
- High: vendors with access to production systems, restricted/PII data, or critical infrastructure.

Onboarding checklist (minimal required artifacts)
- Statement of Work / Contract signed.
- Security questionnaire completed and assessed.
- Insurance and SOC/ISO/Attestation (as required by risk level).
- Data handling addendum (if access to any customer or restricted data).
- Onboarding runbook with contact list and escalation path.

Operational controls after onboarding
- Quarterly vendor risk revalidation.
- Contract milestones and SLAs tracked in Vendor Registry.
- Offboarding: revoke accesses, archive logs, verify data return/deletion.

6) Travel & Expense Guidelines (concise)

Booking and approvals
- Use the preferred travel vendor portal for flights and hotels. Same-day upgrades and luxury-class travel require VP approval. Train travel < 4 hours is preferred where available.

Per diem and reimbursements
- Domestic per diem: $75/day for meals and incidental expenses.
- International per diem: varies by region; use Finance per diem lookup.
- Receipts required for any single item > $25.

Expense submission timeline
- Submit expenses within 14 calendar days of trip completion. Finance audit reserves the right to request more documentation and to withhold reimbursement if policy not followed.

7) Templates, Forms & Automation Links

- Access Request Form: /confluence/forms/access-request (use for all access changes).
- Procurement Request Template: /confluence/forms/procurement-request.
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (spreadsheet template).
- Change Request RFC template: /confluence/templates/change-rfc.

Appendix A: Approval matrices (quick reference)
| Action | Approver(s) | Max Escalation SLA | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Grant Admin Access | Manager + Security-Admin | 48 hours | Timebox to 7 days unless renewed |
| Standard Procurement (<5k) | Manager | 48 hours | Auto-approve if budget available |
| Vendor Risk Review (Medium) | Procurement + Security | 5 business days | Use standard questionnaire |
| Emergency Infra Change | SRE on-call + Service Owner | Immediate (log within 2 hours) | Post-change RFC required |

Appendix B: Contacts and ownership

- Finance approvals: finance-approvals@redwood.com

Governance & review cadence
- This playbook will be reviewed biannually by Finance + Security + People Ops. Major changes require an RFC and signoff by VP of Finance and Head of Security.
